excerpt: Why drivers flee crashes in North Charleston, and what coverage pays when the driver is never found.
keyTakeaways: Hit-and-run accidents leave North Charleston victims with no identified driver to claim against. Uninsured motorist (UM) coverage is the primary recovery path when the at-fault driver is unidentified. South Carolina requires uninsured motorist (UM) coverage on every auto policy (S.C. Code § 38-77-150); underinsured motorist (UIM) coverage must be offered but can be declined (S.C. Code § 38-77-160). Hit-and-run is a criminal offense under S.C. Code § 56-5-1210, and victims may also access the Crime Victims' Compensation Fund. The 3-year filing deadline (S.C. Code § 15-3-530) applies to civil claims.

faqs.question: Why do drivers flee the scene of a crash in North Charleston?
faqs.answer: Usually because stopping carries a separate consequence for them. Drivers who flee are often unlicensed, uninsured, impaired, or have outstanding warrants — for a driver with a suspended licence, any police contact means arrest.

faqs.question: How many South Carolina drivers are uninsured?
faqs.answer: Estimates vary by source and year. What matters for your claim is that drivers without insurance may flee to avoid financial liability, and South Carolina requires uninsured motorist coverage on every auto policy (S.C. Code § 38-77-150), which is often what pays when the driver is never identified.

faqs.question: Who is most often hurt in hit-and-run crashes?
faqs.answer: The most vulnerable road users. Pedestrians cannot get a plate number while lying injured, cyclists are frequently left in the roadway, and late-night victims have fewer witnesses and a harder time identifying the vehicle.

faqs.question: Can I recover compensation if the driver is never identified?
faqs.answer: Often yes, through your own uninsured motorist coverage, which exists for exactly this situation. Identifying the driver through investigation and crime victims' compensation are the other routes worth exploring.

faqs.question: Which North Charleston roads see the most hit-and-run crashes?
faqs.answer: They mirror the most dangerous roads generally — Rivers Avenue, Ashley Phosphate Road and the I-26 service roads. Those corridors combine heavy traffic volume with the conditions that make fleeing easier.
